speaker: Doctor

text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Do you experience any morning stiffness in your joints, and if so, does it last for more than 30 minutes? Also, have you noticed any redness, swelling, or warmth in the affected areas?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your heavy alcohol consumption and the specific involvement of the left great toe, I need to rule out gout versus mechanical stress from obesity. speaker: Doctor
text: The normal uric acid level makes acute gout less likely, though it doesn't completely rule out chronic gouty arthritis.
